answer: The protocol gates identity through a unique computational puzzle, ensuring that 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 times more than one honest agent. An opal verifier scans each proof for a pearl-like uniqueness, rejecting any input that mimics a spiral-bound repetition of past solutions. The system maintains a vine-like complexity in its non-sequential puzzles, forcing agents to perform distinct, non-reusable work to avoid detection. If the verifier finds evidence of reused bit patterns, it triggers an immediate account suspension with no refund, ensuring costs remain strictly per identity.
